column2: The elapsed days and the Lord's rest from all surrounding enemies precede Joshua's old age; both temporal clauses and the advanced-in-days image remain.
All Israel, council of elders, leaders, scribes and judges are summoned; Joshua repeats the narrator's old-age description in his own voice.
Israel has seen the Lord's deeds to all the nations, and the Lord is identified as the one who fought for them; agency and repeated title remain.
Behold, the remaining nations assigned by tribal lots, Jordan, destroyed nations and future Great Sea/sunset boundary remain without flattening the selected clause sequence.
column3: The boundary subject and the relationship between remaining and destroyed nations are compressed; inherited punctuation is provisional, not a reconstructed map.

column2: The Lord's destruction promise includes the selected wild beasts and kings, followed by the command to inherit; no beast clause is omitted or made a metaphor without evidence.
Great strength is directed toward keeping and doing everything written in Moses' law book, with the negative purpose of turning neither right nor left preserved.
Avoiding entry among the remaining nations, naming their gods, bowing and service remain distinct prohibitions. No oath clause absent from the selected text is imported.
Clinging to the Lord contrasts with foreign service and is linked to conduct until this day; the inherited imperative represents the exhortative future in context.
The Lord's past destruction of great strong nations and no one standing against Israel until this day remain separate assertions.
One pursuing a thousand remains past narrative, explained by the Lord's fighting for Israel as promised; it is not converted into a future numerical promise.
Great care to love the Lord remains the complete short exhortation; no extra soul phrase is supplied.
The condition includes turning back, attachment to remaining nations, intermarriage and reciprocal mingling, ending before the result in the next unit.
The emphatic cessation of divine destruction leads to traps, stumbling blocks, heel-nails and eye-darts until loss of the good land; the selected concrete images remain.
Joshua's departure follows the way of everyone on earth; future knowledge in heart and soul confirms that no word failed or proved untrue, preserving both negative fulfillment statements.
column3: All that belongs to you represents ta anekonta hymin; all that concerns you is a possible broader rendering needing contextual assessment rather than an assumption of property alone.

column2: All good words arriving are matched by all harmful words the Lord will bring, until destruction from the good land; the good/harmful word contrast is retained.
Transgressing the commanded covenant and going to serve and bow to other gods completes the preceding warning; no additional wrath or rapid-perishing sentence is added.
Joshua assembles all tribes at the selected Shiloh, summons elders, scribes and judges and makes them stand before God; Shiloh is not changed to Shechem.
Joshua introduces the Lord's first-person speech, recalling fathers beyond the River, Terah's two father relations and service of other gods.
God takes Abraham, leads him through all the land, multiplies offspring and gives Isaac; the source does not specify Canaan in the all-the-land phrase here.
Jacob and Esau are given to Isaac, Seir to Esau, and Jacob's household goes to Egypt and becomes a great, numerous, mighty nation. All three qualities remain.
Egyptian affliction is followed by the Lord striking and bringing Israel out; the source shifts from divine I to third person, and the inherited inner quotation closes before this unit.
Out of Egypt completes the previous clause; Israel enters the Red Sea and Egyptian chariots and horses pursue the fathers into it, preserving both sea mentions.
The selected we cried and between us shift the person, while your eyes and you in the wilderness return to plural audience language. Cloud, thick darkness and the sea covering remain.
The Lord brings Israel to the trans-Jordan Amorites and delivers them, while Israel inherits and destroys them; the human and divine actions remain differentiated.
Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arrays against Israel and calls Balaam to curse; this selected conflict description is not harmonized to another narrative's wording.
The Lord is unwilling to destroy the addressee, blesses abundantly, rescues and hands them over; no unwillingness-to-listen-to-Balaam wording is substituted.
column3: The opening your/you is singular, then blessing/rescue use plural you. The antecedent of final them and the beneficiary of the final handing over remain implicit.

column2: Jericho's inhabitants and seven named peoples fight Israel before the Lord's deliverance; Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, Hittites and Girgashites keep their selected order.
The wasp swarm drives out twelve Amorite kings, not two; the final sword/bow belongs to a singular collective addressee after plural before you.
column3: The precise collective force of sphekia and the implicit subject of drove out remain lexical/syntactic questions; the selected twelve is not altered.

column2: Unlaboured land and unbuilt cities are gifts, with settlement in the plural cities. The vineyards and olive groves culminate in future you shall eat, not a present-tense paraphrase.
Fear, service in uprightness and righteousness, removal of foreign gods and repeated service remain; the fathers' River and Egypt locations are both retained.
The conditional displeasure, explicit for-yourselves choice, two god groups and Joshua's household declaration remain, including the selected for He is holy ending.
The people reject abandoning the Lord for other gods with may it never be; the negative wish and purpose relationship remain.
The Lord our God is explicitly God, brought us and our fathers out and guarded the whole journey among all nations; no sign or slave-house clauses absent here are inserted.
The Lord expelled the Amorites and all inhabiting nations; the people's reciprocal pledge and He is our God explanation remain.
Joshua's emphatic cannot serve, God's holiness and jealousy, and refusal to forgive both sins and lawless deeds remain without softening the warning.
Whenever abandonment and other-god service occur, the Lord comes, afflicts and consumes in return for prior good; the conditional timing and reversal remain.
The people's No rejects Joshua's warning and is followed by their service pledge; English sentence division conveys the adversative response without changing its speaker.
The people are witnesses against themselves for choosing the Lord; the speech continues directly into 24:23 without an inserted we are witnesses response.
Removal of gods among them and directing their heart to the Lord complete Joshua's exhortation; the collective singular heart is retained.
The people promise service and obedience to His voice; the Lord is fronted in the inherited sentence to retain the selected focus.
Joshua establishes covenant, law and judgment that day at Shiloh before God's tent; the selected location and sanctuary description remain.
The words are written in a scroll, the law of God, and a great stone is set beneath the terebinth before the Lord; no different tree or expanded sanctuary clause is substituted.
The stone hears words spoken to it by the Lord, bears testimony among the people now and at the last of the days, and witnesses false dealing with the Lord my God. The personification and my remain.
column3: The relationship of spoken to it to spoken to us is deliberately retained rather than harmonized; the final temporal expression is not expanded into a doctrinal explanation.

column2: Joshua dismisses the people and each goes to his own place; the distributive each remains.
Israel's service throughout Joshua's and the surviving elders' days precedes the death notice in this selected order; their seeing the Lord's works remains explicit.
Joshua son of Nun, servant of the Lord, dies at one hundred ten after these things; this unit is not renumbered to another textual ordering.
Burial at his allotment's borders retains Thamnathasachara, Ephraim's mountain and the northern relation to Mount Gaash; the longer selected place spelling remains distinct from Thamnasarach.
The tomb receives the stone knives used at Gilgal; the selected when he brought them out of Egypt, Lord's command and present-day preservation all remain in the lettered unit.
column3: The subject and chronology of brought them out are difficult in context; no Moses substitution or reconstructed chronology is inserted.

column2: Joseph's bones are brought from Egypt and buried at Shechem in Jacob's acquired field portion, bought from resident Amorites for one hundred ewe lambs and given to Joseph; no money unit is substituted.
Eleazar son of Aaron the high priest dies after these things and is buried at his son Phinehas' Gabaath in Ephraim's mountain; the giving clause remains.
column3: The unstated subject of he had given him is not resolved by adding a named donor.

column2: Israel carries the ark about among themselves, and Phinehas succeeds Eleazar until his own death and burial at his Gabaath; the entire selected continuation remains.

Return to each place and city precedes service of Astarte, Ashtaroth and surrounding gods, then the Lord's handing over to Eglom of Moab for eighteen years. The longer ending is not removed or harmonized to Judges.
